title: Resolution pullback of global cohomology respects boundary maps for geometric morphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to a common sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], with inverse image $L=f^{-1}$ and direct image $f_*$. Use the induced exact inverse image on abelian sheaves. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C$, write $\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(F)=\operatorname{Hom}(*,F)$ and $H^q(\mathcal C,F)=R^q\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(F)$; similarly on $\mathcal D$. For injective resolutions $F\to I^\bullet$ and $LF\to J^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], a comparison $\beta:LI^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ extending the identity of $LF$ exists. The maps $P_f^q(F):H^q(\mathcal C,F)\to H^q(\mathcal D,LF)$ induced by $\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\eta}\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(f_*LI^\bullet)\cong\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(LI^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(\beta)}\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(J^\bullet)$ are independent of both resolutions and of $\beta$, natural in $F$, and in degree zero send a global section $s:*\to F$ to $Ls:*\cong L*\to LF$. For every short exact sequence $E:0\to F\to F'\to F''\to0$, its exact image $LE$ satisfies $P_f^{q+1}(F)\,\delta_E^q=\delta_{LE}^q\,P_f^q(F'')$ for all $q\geq0$. For every morphism $(a,b,c):E\to E'$ of short exact sequences on either site, $H^{q+1}(a)\delta_E^q=\delta_{E'}^qH^q(c)$. The maps $\delta$ here are the connecting homomorphisms of the derived global-section long exact sequences. The identifications $\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(f_*M)=\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(M)$ use adjunction and $L*\cong *$. No final site object and no functor between the presenting sites are assumed.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ and $G=\Gamma_{\mathcal C}$, $T=\Gamma_{\mathcal D}$. Global sections are additive: their addition is pointwise addition of maps into an abelian group object. They preserve kernels, since a map from the terminal sheaf lands in a kernel exactly when its composite with the defining map is zero. Thus $G,T$ are left exact additive. Adjunction and the finite-limit preservation in the geometric-morphism datum give $\operatorname{Hom}(*,f_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L*,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(*,M)$. Under this bijection the unit defines a natural additive map $t_M:G(M)\to T(LM)$ sending $s$ to $Ls$ after $*\cong L*$. This also defines a natural map of complexes $t_K:G(K)\to T(LK)$. No representing terminal object of either site is used.

source.place: Tag 01FT (section-cohomology-sheaves), global sections without a final site object; adjunction calculation

proof.text: Both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are abelian with enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]; take nonnegative injective resolutions, whose augmentations and degree-zero identifications are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]. Exactness of the given $L$ makes $LF[0]\to LI^\bullet$ a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] with $K=LF[0]$, $L^\bullet=LI^\bullet$, target $J^\bullet$, and $\gamma$ the target augmentation. It gives $\beta:LI^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ strictly over $LF$. Therefore the chain map $w_{I,J}=T(\beta)t_I:G(I^\bullet)\to T(J^\bullet)$ gives the claimed map on cohomology under the resolution identifications.

Any two choices of $\beta$ agree after the quasi-isomorphism $LF[0]\to LI$ and hence are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]; applying $T$ and then cohomology gives equal maps by [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology]. More generally, for $h:F\to F'$ and resolutions $(I,J)$, $(I',J')$, choose augmented lifts $u:I\to I'$ of $h$ and $v:J\to J'$ of $Lh$ by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]. The maps $v\beta$ and $\beta'Lu$ from $LI$ to $J'$ have the same composite with $LF[0]\to LI$; the same uniqueness lemma makes them homotopic. Naturality of $t$ gives $t_{I'}G(u)=T(Lu)t_I$, so on cohomology $H^q(Tv)H^q(w_{I,J})=H^q(w_{I',J'})H^q(Gu)$. The map-via-lift formula of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] identifies the two outer maps with $H^q(Lh)$ and $H^q(h)$. This proves naturality. For $h=1_F$ it proves independence of both resolutions, since the same formula identifies the resolution changes with the canonical identity maps on $R^qG(F)$ and $R^qT(LF)$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero], $G(F)\to H^0(GI)$ and $T(LF)\to H^0(TJ)$ are the canonical isomorphisms induced by the augmentations. The augmented square for $w_{I,J}$ commutes, because $\beta$ is over $LF$ and $t$ is natural. Consequently its degree-zero map is $t_F$, which step 1 computed as $s\mapsto Ls$ with domain identified using $*\cong L*$.

Fix a short exact sequence $E$ and choose a horseshoe $I_1\to I_2\to I_3$ by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]. Every row splits by [lem-weil-pbc-ses-injective-kernel-splits]. Its images under $G$ and under $TL$ therefore split: applying an additive functor to $pi=1$, $rs=1$, $ip+sr=1$ gives the same splitting equations. In particular both image sequences are degreewise short exact; extension by zero remains so. We identify precisely which boundary $\partial_I$ on $H^q(GI_3)$ this computes. In the derived category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-sc-p1-horseshoe-derived-triangle-comparison] gives a triangle morphism from $RG(E[0])$ to the derived triangle of $G(I)$, with endpoint homology maps $j_{I_i}\theta_{F_i}$. By boundary naturality in [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] and the snake/derived identification of [lem-sc-p1-nat-complex-derived-boundary], its endpoint equation is $j_{I_1}^{q+1}\delta_E^q=\partial_I^q j_{I_3}^q$, after the single-object identifications $\theta$. Thus this is the derived global-section connecting map specified in the item. The identical application to $T$ identifies $\delta_{LE}$ with the boundary of any target horseshoe $J_1\to J_2\to J_3$. All these applications have enough injectives by step 2, left exactness by step 1, and the required image exactness by the splitting equations just given.

Choose a target horseshoe $J$ resolving $LE$ as in step 5. The source row $LI_1\to LI_2\to LI_3$ has exact augmented columns, since $L$ is exact, and short exact rows, since its original rows split. The lifting argument of step 2 gives endpoint maps $\beta_1:LI_1\to J_1$, $\beta_3:LI_3\to J_3$ over the identity maps of $LF_1,LF_3$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] to this augmented source row and the target horseshoe, with morphism $1_{LE}$. It supplies $\beta_2$ making both row squares commute strictly and preserving the middle augmentation. Here no $LI_i^n$ is required to be injective. The maps $w_i=T(\beta_i)t_{I_i}$ consequently give a morphism of short exact complexes $G(I_1\to I_2\to I_3)\to T(J_1\to J_2\to J_3)$. Its rows are short exact by step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], $H^{q+1}(w_1)\partial_I^q=\partial_J^q H^q(w_3)$. Step 3 identifies its endpoint maps with the specified $P_f$, independently of these convenient choices, and step 5 identifies its boundaries with the derived $\delta_E,\delta_{LE}$. Substitution proves $P_f^{q+1}(F_1)\delta_E^q=\delta_{LE}^qP_f^q(F_3)$.

source.place: Horseshoe comparison for exact augmented source columns (Tag 013T construction); homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), naturality

proof.text: For a morphism $(a,b,c):E\to E'$ on either site, apply [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] to that site's global-section functor. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 2, and clause (1) gives $H^{q+1}(a)\delta_H^q=\delta_{H'}^qH^q(c)$ for horseshoe boundaries. Step 5 identifies both of these with the specified derived boundaries. This gives the last assertion on either site. The whole argument used only the geometric adjunction, the terminal sheaf and exactness of its abelian inverse image, so it applies without a functor between the presenting sites or a final object of either site.
